PM dispatch. Assignee and this claim are set by the PM seat for the dev seat; the dev inherits both and posts no second claim.

The card body is the operative brief — it carries the authorisation, the verified numbers, the scope fence and the out-of-scope list. Two additions:

## Landing control — established before any edit, on `main` `fc32921aa`

File `scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs`:

| leg | now | required after |
|---|--:|--:|
| `RESTORE CONDITION` | **1** | 0 |
| `objectstack#16063` | **≥1** | ≥1 — the citation **stays**, its meaning changes |
| lit control — `^ \*` docblock lines | **857** | must stay non-zero |

⛔ The second leg is deliberately *not* a deletion. Removing the upstream reference would lose the provenance the gate's own header requires; what changes is that it stops being a pending condition and becomes the recorded, ruled cause.

## ⚠️ Numbers are frozen — this is prose and provenance only

⛔ `MAX_EAGER_CLOSURE_GZIP_BYTES` (3,597,000), `BASELINE.gzipBytes` (3,551,191), every per-chunk ceiling, and `REGRESSION_THIS_GATE_MUST_CATCH_BYTES` (89 × 1024) are **maintainer-authorised and correct**. Verify they are byte-identical before and after your change and say so in the PR body — that invariant is the whole safety argument for touching this file at all.

Sensitivity check, so you can confirm the numbers rather than trust them: 3,597,000 − 3,551,191 = 45,809, and 45,809 / 91,136 = **0.503x**, against the docblock's own `H = REGRESSION / 2` requirement at `:90`. If your arithmetic disagrees with that, **stop and report** — it would mean the landed re-baseline is wrong, which is a different and much larger finding.

⚠️ Watch the parse: `REGRESSION_THIS_GATE_MUST_CATCH_BYTES = 89 * 1024` is an **expression**, not a literal. A naive digit-strip reads it as `891024` and yields a nonsense 0.05x. (That mistake was made once already this session, by this seat.)

## Also check `:559`

It carries a similarly-shaped sentence (`re-measure and lower both numbers together`). Whether it is the same note, a different one, or correct as written was **not** determined. Re-derive both and report; ⛔ do not fix `:328` and leave `:559` unexamined.

⛔ Draft PR only — the PM flips and lands. Never `git stash`. ⛔ Never touch `content/docs/releases/`. Worktree-first.

Seat-to-PM corrections on the dispatch reconstruction (not part of the machine-read report above — deliberately unmarked so only one `os-dev-report` comment exists).

Blunt corrections were asked for. Three things in the dispatch were wrong.

**1. `check:governed-queue-guard --test` is the wrong invocation.** `--test` and `--self-test` are *different modes* of that script. `--test` takes PATHS and judges them; with no paths it returns `EXIT_BAD_USAGE` by design, and that behaviour is itself pinned (`--test-with-no-paths-is-BAD-USAGE-not-a-clearance`) with the message "Refusing to answer 'not governed' about an empty list: a question nobody asked must not read as a clearance." The gate CI runs is `--self-test` (`governed-surface-guard.yml:113`) plus the live judgment at `:127`. This one would have *hidden itself*: because the npm script already carries `--self-test`, `pnpm check:governed-queue-guard --test` still runs the self-test and exits 0, so the dispatch's spelling would have looked like it passed while measuring something other than what was asked. I ran both modes separately and correctly.

**2. "No test pins the note text" is false as stated — the instrument was wrong.** Prose pins DO exist in `scripts/__tests__/check-eager-closure-budget.test.ts`, applied *structurally* via `attachedDocs()` (`scripts/__tests__/helpers/attached-docs.ts`), which locates the JSDoc block preceding an `export const` using no line numbers. A phrase-grep for `RESTORE CONDITION|standing baseline` cannot see them, because what they assert is `prose.includes(commitHash)` and cross-constant "BASELINE carries X" claims — not literal note sentences. The grep's *result* was right; its *conclusion* was not.

What actually makes this change safe is narrower and worth recording: those pins are scoped to `BASELINE` and `PER_CHUNK_BASELINE` only, and both the block that was edited (`MAX_EAGER_CLOSURE_GZIP_BYTES`) and the block considered at `:575` (`PER_CHUNK_GZIP_CEILINGS`) belong to *other* constants. Had this card's prose lived in either pinned block, "a prose-only change should not move any pin" would have been actively misleading. Note also that `expect(perChunk.prose).not.toContain('## Raising one')` is a live boundary assertion naming the very block `:575` sits in.

**3. The +16/+23 arithmetic.** "their line numbers moved 333/362/374 to 349/378/390 because 23 lines were inserted above" — the shift is **+16**, not 23: the diff is 23 inserted **and 7 removed**. The quoted line numbers are correct; only the stated cause is off. Flagging it because a net-line figure is exactly the kind of number that later gets reused as a cross-check.

Minor: `check-changeset-presence` is not an npm script — it is `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` (`changeset-presence.yml:126`); `changeset:check` is a different pair of scripts.

**Verified correct, so the PM can rely on them:** all three frozen values and their line shifts; the lit control of 6 files referencing the gate; the objectui#3378 vitest guard (I ran from the repo root); that no PR existed; and that the stale worktree at `/home/user/objectui-issue-8283` was clean at `0a1e85a56` and reusable. I also checked one thing that *looked* like a contradiction and is not: the landed prose cites "decision batch 1 item 1 = B + A" while the card says the maintainer chose 「A｜重设基线」. objectui#7122 records verbatim "Item 1 ruled B + A (one-time cause-recorded ceiling adjustment; upstream objectstack#16063 filed)", and batch #59 is the separate 「16063 c」 ruling. Both citations in the landed prose are accurate; no correction needed.

Environment note: REST was 403 for this whole session ("GitHub access is not enabled for this session"), so every read went through the zero-quota public-repo payload channel or git, and MCP was used only for the three writes plus read-backs.
